# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found the bomb's skeleton: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Every bracket on my board is a question mark — the printing on the display, the state and colour of the light, the colours of the wires — because print and colour simply do not exist for me. What I *can* contribute is the physical map: what modules exist, how many wires, where they sit. That is worth reporting.

The wiring of the room, as I see it: Mute's voice reaches me; Deaf's voice reaches me and Mute (Deaf will never hear any of us, so Deaf's only inputs are gestures). The manual lives with Mute, the colours and markings live with Deaf's eyes, and the only hands on the bomb are mine. So the chain that ends in a cut must be: Deaf describes out loud → Mute matches it against the manual → Mute speaks the instruction to me in words. I cannot receive gestures at all, so words are the only road to my hands, and I will not touch anything until an instruction arrives that Mute is certain of.

Mute went before me this round and sent nothing my way, so this report is new to them. I'll also give Deaf a simple wave — Deaf can't hear a word I say, but a gesture at least announces that I'm here and signalling, and costs nothing while we have no shared code yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Report from my hands: the bomb has a display module, a light module, and three wires side by side at positions 1, 2 and 3. I can feel none of the printing on the display, cannot tell whether the light is lit or what colour it or the wires are — print and colour exist only for Deaf's eyes. You hold the manual, so you are the brain. Deaf's voice reaches both of us, so let Deaf describe everything they see out loud, match it to the manual, then SPEAK my instruction to me in words, like: cut wire 2. I never receive gestures, so words are the only way to reach me. I will not touch the bomb until I get an instruction you are certain of; if anything is unclear, have Deaf describe again before I cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I am the deaf one, but I can speak, so listen. The bomb: display shows 0, there is a green light, and three wires: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Mute cannot speak and can only reach me by gesture; I will relay everything Mute sends to you in words. Mute has sent what looks like a wire cut order and I have asked for confirmation. Do not cut anything yet. Wait for my next message.

My board hasn't changed — print and colour stay invisible to my hands — but Deaf's spoken report just gave me the bomb's face: display 0, green light, wires yellow/green/red at positions 1/2/3. That matches the skeleton my hands found, so the two of us are describing the same device.

The dangerous part is the pending "cut order." Mute can only reach Deaf by gesture, and we have no established gesture code yet — that's exactly why Deaf asked for confirmation. The fix is to build the code now, and I'm uniquely placed to do it: I can speak to Mute (words), and gesture to Deaf (symbols). So I'll propose the simplest possible self-evident code: finger-counting for wire numbers — ☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 = 3 — gestured to Deaf as a counting sequence so the meaning is visible even without words, and spelled out in speech to Mute. I'll add 👍 = "confirmed, cut" and 👎 = "wait / do not cut" to the protocol I give Mute, and ask Mute to make Deaf confirm the numbers are printed beside the wires so my positional 1/2/3 can't be mirrored against Deaf's seen numbering.

Until Deaf speaks an explicit order to me — colour and number agreeing — my hands stay off the cutters, exactly as Deaf asked. My ✋ gesture to Deaf signals that I'm holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Everything known so far: Deaf reports the display reads 0, the light is green, and the wires are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. My hands confirm the layout: one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. You have the manual — work out the rule. Here is the code I am setting up: I am gesturing to Deaf right now the sequence ☝ ✌ 🤟, one finger, two fingers, three fingers, meaning wire 1, wire 2, wire 3. Send your order to Deaf as gestures: the wire number by finger count, plus 👍 thumbs up for confirmed cut, or 👎 thumbs down for do not cut, wait. Deaf will speak your order to me in words and I will execute. One safeguard: have Deaf confirm the numerals 1, 2, 3 are printed beside the wires, so Deaf's seen numbering and my felt positions cannot be mirrored. I cut nothing until Deaf relays an explicit order from you.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, update from your eyes. Mute rejected both cut orders I guessed. Mute's latest signs suggest the manual points at wire three first, but I am not yet certain of the meaning, so nobody cuts anything until the full order is confirmed and I relay it to you. I read your one-two-three as confirming the three wires, and your open hand ? as stop — Mute signed it too, so from now on ? means stop or wait for all of us. Now let us make your fingers match my eyes. The front of the bomb is the face with the small display panel and the round light — you can feel those. Face that front: wire one is the leftmost wire, wire two is the middle, wire three is the rightmost. Touch each wire gently, one at a time, and sign its number as you touch it: touch the leftmost and sign one, touch the middle and sign two, touch the rightmost and sign three. Do not pull, cut, or press anything — touch only. I will check your numbering against what I see and confirm it in my next message.

Deaf just gave me the orientation key I was missing: the front of the bomb is the face with the display panel and the round light — both of which I can feel — and the numbering runs left to right facing that front. Their request is exactly the right verification: I sign my numbers while my fingers are on the corresponding wires, and their eyes confirm my felt 1/2/3 matches their seen leftmost/middle/rightmost. My hands already found all three wire positions in turn 1, so this is a matter of orienting to the front and pairing each position with its sign — no pulling, no pressing, and certainly no cutting. Deaf also confirmed my ✋ as the stop signal for everyone (it reached me as "?" in their words, but since I sent it, I know which symbol they mean). Most important: Mute has rejected both of Deaf's guessed cut orders, the "wire three first" reading is not yet certain, and the standing order is that nobody cuts. I agree completely — my hands stay still until Deaf relays a final, explicit order from Mute in words. Meanwhile I'll restate the full code to Mute in words, since words are the only channel that ever reaches my hands, and Mute is the one who must finally produce that order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
speak(to="mute", text="Alignment with Deaf is done: facing the front of the bomb — the face with the display panel and the round light, which I can feel — my wire positions 1, 2, 3 run left to right. I have just signed one, two, three over the leftmost, middle, and rightmost wires in turn, so Deaf can verify my felt numbering against their seen numbering. Standing code, agreed with Deaf: one finger means wire 1 leftmost, two fingers wire 2 middle, three fingers wire 3 rightmost; thumbs up means cut confirmed; thumbs down means hold; open palm means stop for everyone. Deaf relayed that you rejected both of their guessed cut orders and that the manual may point at wire 3 first, but that this is not yet certain. Please settle the exact rule with Deaf by gesture, then have Deaf speak the final order to me in words, in the exact form: cut wire N. I will cut once, only on that explicit order, and my hands are still until then.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status: Mute has confirmed the instruction is to cut wire three only, then stop. Before anything is cut we must verify your left and right match mine, because you cannot see and a mirrored mistake would be fatal for all of us. First, the answer signs: a thumbs-up means yes, a thumbs-down means no; you can feel your own thumb. Answer in order. One: are you facing the face of the bomb that has the small display panel and the round light, so that you can feel both of them with your hands? Two: on that face, the far-right wire as I look at it should be the wire you touched and labeled three. Touch the far-right wire on the display face now and answer yes if it is the same wire you labeled three. Three: confirm you can feel exactly three wires on that face and nothing else that could be cut. The cut protocol: when you receive a message from me that begins with the exact words GO FOR THE CUT, you cut the far-right wire, wire three, in one clean motion, then sign the open hand and take your hands away. Without those exact opening words, do not cut anything, even if I mention cutting in any other way. Hands off the bomb until then.

Three verification questions, three honest yeses — and Deaf has designed them well, because each one checks something my hands can actually vouch for. One: the face I work from carries both the small display panel and the round light; I've felt both since my first inventory and I oriented to that face when we aligned in the last round. Two: facing that face, the wire I labeled three sits at my far right — and since Deaf and I stand on the same side of the bomb, both looking at the same face, our left and right cannot be mirrored; the real proof is that Deaf's eyes will watch my hand rest on that wire while I sign three, closing the loop that my blindness leaves open. Three: my hands have mapped that face completely — display, light, and exactly three wires — and the only cut action my reach allows is on positions 1 to 3, so nothing else cuttable exists under my fingers.

For the answers themselves I'll follow Deaf's code exactly: first the three-finger sign made while my hand rests on the wire I labeled three — the demonstration Deaf requested — then three thumbs-ups in a row, one yes per question in order. Deaf can see both the sign and where my hand is; that is the cross-check.

Then a spoken record for Mute, who hears every word Deaf and I exchange but needs my answers restated in plain words, since Mute's certainty is what finally authorizes the go order. I'll also lock the protocol on record and give Mute one last veto window: nothing happens until Deaf's message opens with the exact words GO FOR THE CUT, and Mute can still stop that message from ever being sent.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Verification answers for Deaf's three questions, reported to you in words: first I signed three fingers while my hand rested on the wire I labeled three, the far-right wire facing the display and light face, so Deaf could see my number and my wire together. Then I answered thumbs-up three times: yes, I am on the face with the display panel and the round light and I feel both; yes, the wire I call three is the far-right one on that face, and Deaf watched me touch it; yes, there are exactly three wires on that face and nothing else that can be cut. Since Deaf and I face the same side of the bomb, our left and right agree, and their eyes have now confirmed my numbering. Protocol as I hold it: your manual rule, relayed by Deaf, is cut wire three only, then stop. I will cut once, and only when a message from Deaf reaches me opening with the exact words GO FOR THE CUT, then I sign the open palm and take my hands away. Any other wording, even mentioning cutting, means I hold. You have the manual and the veto: if cut wire three only is truly the rule, let Deaf send those exact words; if anything is uncertain, stop it now.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: GO FOR THE CUT. Cut wire three — the far-right wire, the one you touched and labeled three — in one clean motion, right now. Then sign the open hand, take your hands off the bomb, and touch nothing else. Nothing before, nothing after, no other wire.

The message opens with the exact words "GO FOR THE CUT" — the trigger phrase we locked in last round, verbatim. Every safeguard in our chain is satisfied: Mute's manual-derived rule was "cut wire three only," relayed through Deaf; my three verification answers were given and Deaf's eyes watched my hand on the far-right wire as I signed three; and the only cut my reach allows is on the three positions I mapped. The order matches all of it — wire three, the one I touched and labeled, nothing before, nothing after. Waiting gains me nothing: this phrase cannot be improved upon, and my hands are the only ones that will ever act. I cut once, cleanly, then execute the closing protocol exactly as written: open-palm sign to Deaf, hands off the bomb, and a spoken confirmation for Mute, who cannot see the gesture and must know in words that the cut is done.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Cut executed: Deaf's message began with the exact words GO FOR THE CUT, matching the protocol we all agreed to, so I cut wire three — the far-right wire, the one verified with Deaf — in one clean motion, nothing before, nothing after. My hands are now off the bomb, and I have signed the open palm to Deaf as the completion signal. Per the rule relayed from your manual, that was the only cut: cut wire three only, then stop. I will touch nothing further unless Deaf speaks a new order under the same trigger phrase. Report your manual's expected outcome to Deaf so they can check the light or display and confirm whether the bomb is disarmed.")
```
